events.title: Core HTTP semantic conventions stabilize
events.detail: v1.23.0 is the first release with stable core HTTP conventions, following the v1.20.0 compatibility baseline and the v1.21.0 feature freeze and transition plan. Earlier experimental HTTP and networking names were already being replaced before stabilization; preserving legacy instrumentation defaults is governed by the migration plan.

events.title: Core database conventions reach release candidate
events.detail: The core database conventions reach release candidate after the experimental schema changes. This is a maturity milestone for the shared database model; database-specific conventions can have different stability levels.

events.title: The database core stabilizes
events.detail: The release notes call this the first release where the core of database semantic conventions has stabilized; selected systems, including MariaDB, Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL, and PostgreSQL, are stable.

events.title: Core RPC, gRPC, and Dubbo conventions reach release candidate
events.detail: Core RPC, gRPC, and Apache Dubbo conventions reach release candidate after the migration from the v1.37.0 baseline. The release also publishes the RPC migration guide. Earlier changes unified response status and method naming; this does not make every RPC system stable.

events.title: JVM metrics become stable
events.detail: The core JVM runtime metrics are marked stable. Experimental JVM metrics remain separately documented; this milestone does not cover TLS, networking, or other runtime domains.

events.title: CPython garbage-collector metrics are introduced
events.detail: CPython-specific garbage-collector metrics enter the conventions, covering collections, collected objects, and uncollectable objects. This milestone concerns garbage collection, not all Python runtime telemetry.

events.title: Selected Kubernetes and container attributes reach alpha
events.detail: A selected set of Kubernetes and container attributes used by Collector components targeting stability is promoted to alpha. This is a scoped maturity transition, not a status change for the entire Kubernetes domain.

events.title: Selected Kubernetes and container registry attributes stabilize
events.detail: Selected Kubernetes and container attributes in the semantic-convention registry are promoted to stable. This does not stabilize all Kubernetes entities or metrics; CPU and memory metric sets have separate release-candidate milestones.

events.title: Process attributes reach release candidate
events.detail: Process attributes are promoted to release candidate. Process metrics and the process entity follow in v1.43.0; this event does not claim that system CPU metrics have reached release candidate.

events.title: Messaging gains Kafka metric conventions
events.detail: Kafka metrics are added as an early specialized messaging surface, before the messaging model is later generalized and reshaped.

events.title: Experimental Kafka metrics are removed
events.detail: The experimental Kafka metric conventions are removed rather than carried forward unchanged, an example of release history that is not simply additive.

events.title: Messaging operations and metric names are generalized
events.detail: Messaging adopts a common operation model with operation names and types. Publish and receive duration metrics are unified into messaging.client.operation.duration, and consumed-message metrics are shared across receive and process operations. This is a cross-system model change after the v1.24.0 compatibility baseline.

events.title: Version-control-system metrics are introduced
events.detail: VCS metrics enter the semantic-conventions surface, followed by resource conventions and continued repository metadata refinement.

events.title: CI/CD and VCS resource conventions arrive
events.detail: The release adds CI/CD resources and spans plus VCS resources, extending the timeline beyond runtime telemetry into delivery and software lifecycle systems.

events.title: CI/CD and VCS conventions reach release candidate
events.detail: CI/CD spans, metrics, logs, attributes, and entities reach release candidate. VCS attributes, entities, and metrics are also promoted. This milestone covers the delivery conventions; process metrics have a separate event.

events.title: GraphQL semantic conventions are introduced
events.detail: GraphQL joins the growing set of protocol and application-specific convention areas.

events.title: Feature-flag conventions are introduced
events.detail: Feature-flag evaluation becomes a first-class event-oriented convention area.

events.title: Profiling semantic conventions are introduced
events.detail: Profile conventions enter the repository, expanding the model beyond traces, metrics, logs, and resources.

events.title: Browser web-vital events are introduced
events.detail: A browser.web_vital event convention is introduced, adding a performance-event signal to the browser resource attributes introduced in v1.12.0.

events.title: A browser document entity is introduced
events.detail: The browser.document entity describes the current document separately from the browser runtime. Its URL can change on navigation while browser runtime attributes remain unchanged. This is an experimental entity introduction, not browser stabilization.

events.title: Generative-AI client conventions are introduced
events.detail: A dedicated gen_ai client surface enters the core repository, starting a fast-moving domain that later gets its own repository.

events.title: GenAI input and output content moves to log-based events
events.detail: The experimental GenAI content model changes from gen_ai.prompt and gen_ai.completion span attributes to log-based input/output events. The old attributes are deprecated. This changes how content is represented across signals, rather than only renaming an attribute.

events.title: GenAI chat content moves to structured attributes
events.detail: Per-message chat events are deprecated in favor of structured system-instruction, input-message, and output-message attributes on spans or an inference-operation-details event. This replaces the earlier content-event model after the v1.36.0 compatibility baseline. Content capture remains opt-in.

events.title: Core gen_ai conventions are deprecated and moved to a dedicated repository
events.detail: All gen_ai.* conventions are deprecated in the core repository as the GenAI work moves to its dedicated semantic-conventions repository. This is a repository migration, not the end of GenAI conventions.

events.title: HTTP client and server conventions enter the specification
events.detail: HTTP client and server span conventions move from working drafts into the main OpenTelemetry specification. HTTP material was already imported on 13 May 2019; this milestone dates entry into the main spec, not the invention of HTTP telemetry.

events.title: Database client conventions enter the specification
events.detail: Database client span conventions move from the working draft into the main specification, including db.type, db.instance, db.statement, and db.user. The draft was imported on 13 May 2019; the displayed interval starts at entry into the main spec.

events.title: gRPC conventions enter the specification
events.detail: gRPC client/server span and message-event conventions move into the main specification. A gRPC draft was imported on 13 May 2019. General RPC conventions follow on 17 June 2020; this is the gRPC origin, not an assertion that generic RPC was already defined.

events.title: Messaging span conventions enter the specification
events.detail: A dedicated messaging-system convention defines spans and messaging.* attributes for systems such as Kafka, RabbitMQ, and ActiveMQ. Earlier imported OpenTracing material described message_bus.destination and producer/consumer spans; this dates the OpenTelemetry messaging convention, not the first messaging tracing concept.

events.title: Kubernetes resource conventions enter the specification
events.detail: Kubernetes resource labels enter the main specification, including cluster, namespace, pod, and deployment names. These build on OpenCensus resource conventions already imported as working material on 13 May 2019. The origin concerns resource attributes, not Kubernetes metrics.

events.title: JVM memory metrics are added
events.detail: The changelog records JVM memory runtime conventions in v1.9.0. This starts the selected memory-to-stability history, not all JVM telemetry history.

events.title: Browser attributes are introduced
events.detail: The browser.* attributes appear in v1.12.0; web vitals follow almost three years later.

events.title: RPC conventions extend beyond gRPC
events.detail: The specification adds common remote procedure call conventions, rpc.system and rpc.method, and support for non-gRPC systems. This extends the gRPC-specific conventions that entered the specification in June 2019.

events.title: HTTP de facto baseline v1.20.0 is released
events.detail: The HTTP migration notice identifies v1.20.0 (or earlier) as the experimental conventions used by existing instrumentations. It preserves their existing defaults and offers http and http/dup opt-ins for migration to stable HTTP and networking conventions.

events.title: Database de facto baseline v1.24.0 is released
events.detail: The database migration notice identifies v1.24.0 (or earlier) as the experimental conventions used by existing instrumentations. It preserves defaults within their existing major version and offers database and database/dup opt-ins for migration to stable conventions.

events.title: Messaging de facto baseline v1.24.0 is released
events.detail: The messaging migration notice identifies v1.24.0 (or earlier) as the experimental conventions used by existing instrumentations. It calls for preserving defaults until stabilization, with messaging and messaging/dup opt-ins for migration.

events.title: RPC de facto baseline v1.37.0 is released
events.detail: The RPC migration notice identifies v1.37.0 (or earlier) as the experimental conventions used by existing instrumentations. It preserves defaults within their existing major version and defines rpc and rpc/dup opt-ins for migration.

events.title: System metrics de facto baseline v1.21.0 is released
events.detail: The system metrics notice identifies v1.21.0 (or earlier) as the conventions used by existing instrumentations and collectors. It asks them to defer breaking changes until system conventions stabilize and provide an opt-in control once the migration plan is finalized.

events.title: Process metrics de facto baseline v1.21.0 is released
events.detail: The OS process metrics notice identifies v1.21.0 (or earlier) as the conventions used by existing instrumentations and collectors. It asks them to defer breaking changes until system conventions stabilize and provide an opt-in control once the migration plan is finalized. This concerns OS process metrics, not JVM or other runtime-specific metrics.

events.title: GenAI de facto baseline v1.36.0 is released
events.detail: Before the repository move, the GenAI migration notice identified v1.36.0 (or earlier) as the conventions whose existing defaults should be preserved. The gen_ai_latest_experimental opt-in selects newer experimental conventions; this baseline does not imply GenAI stability.

events.title: HTTP conventions enter feature freeze with a transition plan
events.detail: The initial HTTP convention set is marked frozen while still experimental. The release includes the transition plan for existing instrumentations, preserving legacy defaults while providing http and http/dup opt-ins. This is a pre-stability milestone; the core stabilizes in v1.23.0.

events.title: Selected Kubernetes and container attributes reach release candidate
events.detail: A selected set of Kubernetes and container attributes is promoted to release candidate before the selected registry attributes stabilize in v1.42.0. Kubernetes metrics have their own maturity milestones.

events.title: Kubernetes and container CPU time metrics reach release candidate
events.detail: The k8s.pod.cpu.time, k8s.node.cpu.time, and container.cpu.time metrics are promoted to release candidate. This scoped milestone is independent of the stabilization of selected registry attributes in the same release.

events.title: Process metrics and entity reach release candidate
events.detail: Process metrics and the process entity are promoted to release candidate, following process attributes in v1.42.0. The v1.44.0 changelog refers back to this promotion while adding missing metrics; it is not the release that first introduced the RC status.
events.transition: process metrics and entity → release candidate

events.title: Selected Kubernetes and container memory metrics reach release candidate
events.detail: Selected pod, node, and container memory metrics are promoted to release candidate, including usage, available memory, resident memory, and working-set metrics. This does not promote the entire Kubernetes metric surface.

events.title: JavaScript runtime conventions are introduced
events.detail: JavaScript runtime conventions enter the specification, extending runtime telemetry beyond the JVM surface. This is separate from CloudEvents conventions introduced in the same release.

events.title: CloudEvents span conventions are introduced
events.detail: CloudEvents conventions define attributes for tracing events that follow the CloudEvents specification.

events.title: CLI application execution spans are introduced
events.detail: A span convention for command-line application execution introduces a dedicated CLI telemetry surface.

events.title: Geographic attributes enter the registry
events.detail: The geo namespace introduces reusable geographic attributes. This is an attribute-domain introduction, independent of the CLI span convention added in the same release.
